metadata.scope: PH — NCR + Bulacan, Cavite, Laguna, Rizal, Antipolo, Pampanga
metadata.notes: 37 new careers researched covering maritime, aviation, agriculture, healthcare support, cybersecurity, data science, creative media, hospitality, logistics, skilled trades, criminology, and administrative roles. All are realistic for Filipino SHS/college-bound students in the target regions. No duplicates of existing 20.

careers.title: Welder
careers.learningPath: TESDA SMAW NC I–IV, then build hours for certification. Many welders start with NC II in 3–6 months and upgrade while working.
careers.narrative: You turn raw metal into strong joints that hold buildings, ships, and vehicles together. With a TESDA certificate, you can work locally or abroad where Filipino welders are always in demand. It is a hands-on path that rewards precision and steady practice.
careers.phSalaryNote: Entry: P18,000–P28,000/month; Experienced: P35,000–P60,000/month; OFW: P80,000–P150,000/month
careers.outlook: Consistently in demand for local construction and overseas deployment, especially in the Middle East and shipbuilding.
careers.verificationNotes: Very strong OFW pathway. Distinct from general electrician.

careers.title: Automotive Technician
careers.learningPath: TESDA Automotive Servicing NC I–IV or BS Industrial Technology major in Automotive. Ladderized programs let you earn while upgrading.
careers.narrative: You diagnose and fix the cars, trucks, and motorcycles that keep the country moving. From quick oil changes to complex engine overhauls, your hands-on skills keep vehicles safe and running. TESDA offers a fast track, and many technicians later open their own shops.
careers.phSalaryNote: Entry: P15,000–P25,000/month; Experienced: P28,000–P45,000/month; OFW: P50,000–P90,000/month
careers.outlook: Growing demand with rising vehicle ownership and expansion of service centers in NCR and CALABARZON.
careers.verificationNotes: Distinct from mechanical engineer (design vs repair). Strong TESDA and OFW pathway.

careers.title: HVAC Technician
careers.learningPath: TESDA RAC Servicing NC II or III, then on-the-job training with commercial HVAC firms. Some pursue BS Mechanical Technology.
careers.narrative: In a tropical country, air-conditioning is essential everywhere from homes to malls to data centers. You install, maintain, and repair cooling systems that keep people comfortable and equipment from overheating. It is a practical trade with steady local work and overseas options.
careers.phSalaryNote: Entry: P16,000–P25,000/month; Experienced: P30,000–P50,000/month
careers.outlook: High demand due to tropical climate, commercial building boom, and data center growth in NCR and Cavite.
careers.verificationNotes: RAC Servicing is a core TESDA qualification. Distinct from general electrician.

careers.title: Seafarer / Deck Officer
careers.learningPath: BS Marine Transportation at a MARINA-accredited maritime school, then sea time as a cadet, followed by PRC board exam for Officer-in-Charge of Navigational Watch.
careers.narrative: You help move the world by guiding ships across oceans carrying goods and people. After finishing a maritime degree and earning your sea time, you take the board exam to become a deck officer. Filipino seafarers are among the most sought-after globally, and this career can support a family back home.
careers.phSalaryNote: Cadet: P15,000–P25,000/month; Third Officer: P80,000–P150,000/month; Chief Mate/Captain: P200,000–P500,000/month
careers.outlook: The Philippines supplies roughly 25% of the world's seafarers; demand remains strong despite global shipping cycles.
careers.verificationNotes: Very distinct and PH-specific. BS Marine Transportation is a well-known program. Different from marine engineer (engine room vs deck/navigation).

careers.title: Agricultural Technician
careers.learningPath: TESDA Agricultural Crops Production NC II/III or BS Agriculture. Many start with short TESDA courses and work on farms or agribusiness firms.
educationPaths: TESDA Agricultural Crops Production NC II
careers.narrative: You work with soil, seeds, and science to grow food for the nation and beyond. Whether you manage a farm, advise growers on better yields, or handle post-harvest processing, your work feeds communities. With agriculture modernizing, tech-savvy technicians are needed more than ever.
careers.phSalaryNote: Entry: P15,000–P22,000/month; Experienced: P25,000–P40,000/month
careers.outlook: Growing demand as the Philippines pushes for food security, agribusiness expansion, and sustainable farming.
careers.licensureOrCert: TESDA NC / none for BS Agriculture
careers.verificationNotes: Distinct from agricultural engineer (which requires engineering board). Covers technician and farm management roles.

careers.title: Aircraft Maintenance Technician
careers.learningPath: BS Aircraft Maintenance Technology or TESDA-related aviation courses, then CAAP certification. Requires hands-on training at an approved aviation school.
careers.narrative: You keep planes safe to fly by inspecting engines, airframes, and electronics before every takeoff. Aviation schools in Metro Manila and nearby provinces train you for this high-responsibility role. With Philippine airports expanding, licensed aircraft technicians are in short supply.
careers.phSalaryNote: Entry: P25,000–P35,000/month; Licensed: P40,000–P70,000/month; Senior: P80,000–P120,000/month
careers.outlook: Strong demand due to airport expansions, new airlines, and MRO facilities in Clark and NAIA.
careers.verificationNotes: Distinct from aeronautical engineer (design) and pilot (operation). AMT is hands-on maintenance.

careers.title: Medical Technologist
careers.learningPath: BS Medical Technology/Medical Laboratory Science, then PRC board exam. Some hospitals hire lab assistants with related degrees and provide training.
careers.narrative: You run the lab tests that help doctors find out what is making a patient sick. From blood counts to cultures, your careful work behind the microscope guides treatment decisions. Hospitals and diagnostic centers across NCR always need board-certified med techs.
careers.phSalaryNote: Entry: P22,000–P30,000/month; Experienced: P35,000–P50,000/month
careers.outlook: Steady demand in hospitals, diagnostic labs, and industrial clinics; also a pathway to abroad.
careers.verificationNotes: Distinct from nurse (patient care) and pharmacist (medication). Board exam required.

careers.title: Cybersecurity Analyst
careers.learningPath: BS Information Technology, BS Computer Science, or BS Information Systems, then industry certs like CompTIA Security+, CEH, or CISSP. Experience in IT support is a common starting point.
careers.narrative: You are the digital bodyguard that stops hackers from stealing data and crashing systems. Banks, BPOs, and government agencies in the Philippines urgently need people who can spot threats and lock down networks. It is a brainy, high-paying path that starts with an IT degree and grows with certifications.
careers.phSalaryNote: Entry: P25,000–P35,000/month; Mid: P40,000–P60,000/month; Senior: P80,000–P120,000/month
careers.outlook: One of the fastest-growing IT roles in the Philippines due to digitalization, BPO expansion, and rising cyber threats.
careers.verificationNotes: Distinct from software engineer (builds apps) and data analyst (analyzes data). Focuses on security.

careers.title: Data Scientist
careers.learningPath: BS Statistics, BS Mathematics, BS Computer Science, or BS Data Science, then graduate study or bootcamps. Strong math and programming skills required.
careers.narrative: You dig through massive piles of numbers to find patterns that help companies make smarter decisions. From predicting sales trends to training AI models, your work blends math, coding, and curiosity. It is a premium career path that is growing fast in Philippine BPOs and tech startups.
careers.phSalaryNote: Entry: P30,000–P45,000/month; Mid: P50,000–P80,000/month; Senior: P100,000–P180,000/month
careers.outlook: Rapidly growing in BPO, fintech, e-commerce, and corporate analytics teams across Metro Manila.
careers.verificationNotes: Distinct from data analyst (existing). Data scientist is more advanced, requiring ML and advanced stats.

careers.title: Marine Engineer
careers.learningPath: BS Marine Engineering at a MARINA-accredited school, then sea time and PRC board exam for Marine Engineer Officer.
careers.narrative: You design, build, and maintain the engines and systems that power ships across the ocean. While deck officers navigate, you keep the heart of the vessel running. Filipino marine engineers are globally respected, and the career offers strong salaries and a clear path to becoming a chief engineer.
careers.phSalaryNote: Cadet: P15,000–P25,000/month; Junior Engineer: P80,000–P150,000/month; Chief Engineer: P250,000–P500,000/month
careers.outlook: Strong global demand; the Philippines is a top supplier of seafaring officers and engineers.
careers.verificationNotes: Distinct from seafarer/deck officer (navigation vs engine room) and mechanical engineer (land-based vs marine).

careers.title: Food Technologist
careers.learningPath: BS Food Technology or BS Food Science, then optional PRC licensure as Food Technologist. Many work in manufacturing, R&D, or government inspection.
careers.narrative: You make sure the food on every Filipino table is safe, nutritious, and delicious. From developing new snack flavors to testing shelf life in a lab, you blend science with daily life. Food factories, research institutes, and government agencies need technologists who understand both chemistry and local tastes.
careers.phSalaryNote: Entry: P20,000–P28,000/month; Experienced: P35,000–P50,000/month
careers.outlook: Growing demand in food manufacturing, export processing zones, and government food safety agencies.
careers.licensureOrCert: PRC Board (Food Technologist) - optional but preferred
careers.verificationNotes: Distinct from chef (cooking) and nutritionist (diet planning). Focuses on food science and safety.

careers.title: Environmental Scientist
careers.learningPath: BS Environmental Science, BS Biology, or BS Chemistry, then possible licensure as Environmental Planner (PRC) or Pollution Control Officer (DENR).
careers.narrative: You study air, water, and land to protect communities from pollution and climate change. Whether assessing a new highway's impact or cleaning up a river, your work helps the Philippines grow sustainably. It is a meaningful career for students who love science and nature.
careers.phSalaryNote: Entry: P22,000–P30,000/month; Experienced: P35,000–P55,000/month
careers.outlook: Rising demand due to stricter environmental laws, ESG reporting, and renewable energy projects.
careers.verificationNotes: Distinct from civil engineer (infrastructure). Focuses on assessment, monitoring, and compliance.

careers.title: UI/UX Designer
careers.learningPath: BS Multimedia Arts, BS Information Technology, or BS Computer Science, plus portfolio building through bootcamps and freelance projects.
careers.narrative: You design apps and websites that feel easy and enjoyable to use. By understanding how people think and click, you create layouts, buttons, and flows that make technology less frustrating. Startups and global companies in BGC and Makati hire UI/UX designers who can show a strong portfolio.
careers.phSalaryNote: Entry: P25,000–P35,000/month; Mid: P40,000–P65,000/month; Senior: P80,000–P120,000/month
careers.outlook: High demand in tech startups, BPOs, fintech, and e-commerce companies across NCR.
careers.verificationNotes: Distinct from graphic designer (visual branding) and software engineer (coding). Focuses on user experience design.

careers.title: Game Developer
careers.learningPath: BS Computer Science, BS Information Technology, or BS Entertainment and Multimedia Computing, then portfolio building via game jams and indie projects.
careers.narrative: You build the worlds, characters, and rules that make video games fun to play. From mobile puzzle games to big PC titles, game development mixes creativity with serious coding. The Philippines has a growing game industry, and many developers also work remotely for global studios.
careers.phSalaryNote: Entry: P25,000–P35,000/month; Mid: P45,000–P70,000/month; Senior: P80,000–P150,000/month
careers.outlook: Growing local industry plus strong remote-work opportunities with international game studios.
careers.verificationNotes: Distinct from software engineer (general) and graphic designer (static visuals). Specialized in interactive entertainment.

careers.title: Multimedia Artist
careers.learningPath: BS Multimedia Arts, AB Film, or related arts degree, then portfolio building. Many are self-taught and hired based on demo reels.
careers.narrative: You bring stories to life through animation, video, and digital art. From TV commercials to social media campaigns, your visuals catch eyes and deliver messages. Advertising agencies, production houses, and corporate creative teams in Metro Manila always need fresh multimedia talent.
careers.phSalaryNote: Entry: P18,000–P25,000/month; Mid: P30,000–P50,000/month; Senior: P60,000–P90,000/month
careers.outlook: Strong demand in advertising, digital marketing, broadcast media, and content production.
careers.verificationNotes: Distinct from graphic designer (print/branding focus) and photographer (still images). Broader digital media scope.

careers.title: Journalist
careers.learningPath: AB Journalism, AB Communication, or AB Broadcast Communication, then internship at newsrooms. Some start as stringers or content writers.
careers.narrative: You ask tough questions, dig for facts, and tell stories that keep the public informed and empowered. Whether covering politics, sports, or community issues, your words shape how people understand the world. Newsrooms, online media, and PR firms in Manila offer many entry points.
careers.phSalaryNote: Entry: P20,000–P28,000/month; Experienced: P35,000–P60,000/month
careers.outlook: Evolving from print to digital, but demand remains for credible reporters, fact-checkers, and multimedia journalists.
careers.verificationNotes: Distinct from content creator (existing) which is more social media/influencer focused. Journalism is traditional media and investigative reporting.

careers.title: Interior Designer
careers.learningPath: BS Interior Design, then PRC licensure exam. Some start as design assistants or CAD operators before taking the board.
careers.narrative: You transform empty rooms into beautiful, functional spaces where people live, work, and relax. From choosing colors to planning layouts, you balance art with practicality. Condo developments and office fit-outs in NCR keep interior designers busy year-round.
careers.phSalaryNote: Entry: P20,000–P30,000/month; Licensed: P35,000–P55,000/month; Senior: P60,000–P100,000/month
careers.outlook: Steady demand from residential condos, hospitality projects, and commercial spaces in Metro Manila and nearby provinces.
careers.verificationNotes: Distinct from architect (building design/structural) and graphic designer (2D visual). Focuses on interior spaces.

careers.title: Photographer / Videographer
careers.learningPath: Short courses, AB Film, or BS Multimedia Arts, then portfolio building. Many start as freelancers or studio assistants.
careers.narrative: You capture moments that tell stories without words. From weddings and product shoots to documentary films, your images preserve memories and sell ideas. With a good camera and a strong portfolio, you can freelance or join media teams, ad agencies, or corporate communications.
careers.phSalaryNote: Entry: P18,000–P25,000/month; Freelance: P25,000–P60,000/month; Senior/Commercial: P50,000–P100,000/month
careers.outlook: Strong demand in events, e-commerce product photography, social media content, and corporate video.
careers.verificationNotes: Distinct from graphic designer and multimedia artist. Focuses on capture/production of visual media.

careers.title: Caregiver
careers.learningPath: TESDA Caregiving NC II (6 months), then work experience. Some pursue BS Nursing or related health degrees later.
careers.narrative: You provide comfort, companionship, and daily assistance to elderly people, children, or patients who need extra help. It is a deeply human job that builds trust one day at a time. Filipino caregivers are trusted worldwide, and this TESDA path can lead to local work or overseas placement.
careers.phSalaryNote: Entry: P12,000–P18,000/month; Experienced: P20,000–P30,000/month; OFW: P40,000–P80,000/month
careers.outlook: Very high demand locally for aging population and massive OFW deployment to Canada, Japan, and the Middle East.
careers.verificationNotes: Distinct from nurse (clinical/medical) and social worker (existing). Focuses on non-medical personal care.

careers.title: Midwife
careers.learningPath: BS Midwifery or Licensed Midwife program, then PRC board exam. Some start as nursing aides and specialize.
careers.narrative: You guide mothers through pregnancy and bring new life safely into the world. In barangay health centers and lying-in clinics across the Philippines, midwives are often the first healthcare worker families meet. It is a respected, hands-on profession with steady community demand.
careers.phSalaryNote: Entry: P18,000–P25,000/month; Experienced: P30,000–P45,000/month; OFW: P50,000–P80,000/month
careers.outlook: Consistent demand in rural health units, lying-in clinics, and overseas maternity care settings.
careers.verificationNotes: Distinct from nurse (general care) and doctor. Midwifery is a separate PRC-regulated profession in the PH.

careers.title: Guidance Counselor
careers.learningPath: AB Psychology or BS Psychology, then MA in Guidance and Counseling, then PRC licensure as Guidance Counselor.
careers.narrative: You help students figure out who they are, what they want, and how to handle tough times. Schools need counselors who can listen without judging and guide teens through academic and personal challenges. It is a meaningful career for those who love supporting others.
careers.phSalaryNote: Entry: P22,000–P30,000/month; Experienced: P35,000–P50,000/month
careers.outlook: Required by law in Philippine schools (DepEd/CHED); demand grows as mental health awareness rises.
careers.verificationNotes: Distinct from psychologist (existing) which requires a PhD for clinical practice. Guidance counselor works in schools with MA level.

careers.title: Physical Therapist
careers.learningPath: BS Physical Therapy, then PRC board exam. Some pursue specialization certificates or DPT abroad.
careers.narrative: You help people walk, move, and live without pain after injury, surgery, or illness. From stroke survivors to athletes, your hands and knowledge rebuild strength and confidence. Hospitals, clinics, and sports teams in NCR need more licensed physical therapists.
careers.phSalaryNote: Entry: P22,000–P30,000/month; Experienced: P35,000–P55,000/month; OFW: P80,000–P150,000/month
careers.outlook: Growing demand in rehab centers, sports clinics, and overseas markets (US, Canada, Middle East).
careers.verificationNotes: Distinct from nurse (general care) and doctor. Requires BS Physical Therapy and PRC board.

careers.title: Speech-Language Pathologist
careers.learningPath: BS Speech-Language Pathology, then PRC board exam. Growing field in the Philippines.
careers.narrative: You help children find their voice and adults recover speech after stroke or injury. Your patient, creative sessions turn frustration into communication. As awareness of autism, stroke rehab, and developmental delays grows, so does the need for speech therapists in schools and hospitals.
careers.phSalaryNote: Entry: P25,000–P35,000/month; Experienced: P40,000–P60,000/month
careers.outlook: Rapidly growing demand in special education centers, hospitals, and private therapy clinics.
careers.verificationNotes: Distinct from physical therapist and psychologist. Specialized in communication and swallowing disorders.

careers.title: Nutritionist-Dietitian
careers.learningPath: BS Nutrition and Dietetics, then PRC board exam. Internship in hospitals or food service required.
careers.narrative: You design healthy meals and educate communities about food that heals rather than harms. In hospitals, you plan diets for patients recovering from surgery; in schools, you teach kids why vegetables matter. With lifestyle diseases rising, your expertise keeps families healthier.
careers.phSalaryNote: Entry: P20,000–P28,000/month; Experienced: P35,000–P50,000/month
careers.outlook: Rising demand in hospitals, wellness centers, food manufacturing, and public health programs.
careers.verificationNotes: Distinct from chef (cooking) and food technologist (food science). Focuses on diet and nutrition therapy.

careers.title: Criminology Graduate
careers.learningPath: BS Criminology, then PRC licensure exam. Graduates enter PNP, BFP, BJMP, NBI, or private security management.
careers.narrative: You protect communities by preventing crime, investigating cases, and enforcing the law. Whether wearing a PNP uniform or working behind the scenes in forensic labs, your work keeps streets safer. Criminology is one of the most popular courses in the Philippines for a reason: it offers a clear path to public service.
careers.phSalaryNote: Entry (PO1): P23,000–P29,000/month; Experienced: P35,000–P50,000/month; With allowances: higher
careers.outlook: Consistent demand for PNP, BFP, and private security roles; criminology is a top enrollment course nationwide.
careers.verificationNotes: Very PH-specific and popular. Distinct from lawyer (existing) and social worker (existing). Focuses on law enforcement and crime prevention.

careers.title: Sales Representative
careers.learningPath: Any business-related degree or even SHS graduate with strong communication skills. Sales is performance-based and values results over credentials.
careers.narrative: You connect people with products and services they actually need. From pharmaceuticals to real estate to software, every industry needs persuasive, trustworthy salespeople. If you are outgoing, resilient, and driven by targets, sales can earn you commissions well above a fixed salary.
careers.phSalaryNote: Entry: P18,000–P25,000/month + commissions; Experienced: P40,000–P80,000/month; Top: P100,000+/month
careers.outlook: Universal demand across FMCG, pharma, tech, insurance, and real estate; commission potential is high.
careers.verificationNotes: Distinct from marketing manager (existing) which is strategic/planning. Sales rep is front-line revenue generation.

careers.title: Business Development Manager
careers.learningPath: BS Business Administration, BS Marketing, or BS Economics, then mid-level experience in sales or operations. MBA is common for senior roles.
careers.narrative: You spot new markets, negotiate deals, and find ways for companies to grow bigger and better. Whether launching a new product line or entering a new city, you turn opportunities into revenue. It is a strategic role for students who love competition, networking, and numbers.
careers.phSalaryNote: Entry: P25,000–P35,000/month; Mid: P50,000–P80,000/month; Senior: P100,000–P180,000/month
careers.outlook: Strong demand in BPO, fintech, logistics, and corporate expansion across NCR and CALABARZON.
careers.verificationNotes: Distinct from entrepreneur (existing) and marketing manager (existing). Focuses on strategic growth and partnerships.

careers.title: Real Estate Broker
careers.learningPath: BS Real Estate Management or related business degree, then PRC licensure as Real Estate Broker. Salesperson experience helps before taking the broker exam.
careers.narrative: You match families and investors with properties that fit their dreams and budgets. From condo units in Makati to farmland in Cavite, you know the market and close the deals. With the Philippine property market always active, skilled brokers earn through commissions and build their own client base.
careers.phSalaryNote: Entry: P20,000–P30,000/month + commissions; Experienced: P50,000–P150,000/month; Top: P300,000+/month
careers.outlook: Consistent demand in residential, commercial, and industrial property markets across NCR and nearby provinces.
careers.verificationNotes: Distinct from entrepreneur (general). Requires PRC license. Very practical for NCR students given property boom.

careers.title: Hotel Manager
careers.learningPath: BS Hospitality Management / BS Hotel and Restaurant Management, then climb from front desk or F&B supervisor to manager. Experience matters more than advanced degrees.
careers.narrative: You run the show behind a hotel's front desk, restaurants, and rooms, making sure every guest leaves happy. From boutique inns in Tagaytay to big chains in Makati, hotel managers blend hospitality with business sense. The Philippines' tourism growth means more hotels and more managers are needed.
careers.phSalaryNote: Entry supervisor: P25,000–P35,000/month; Manager: P50,000–P80,000/month; GM: P100,000–P200,000/month
careers.outlook: Tourism rebound and new hotel openings in NCR, Cebu, and leisure destinations drive steady demand.
careers.verificationNotes: Distinct from chef (existing) and restaurant manager. Hotel manager oversees full property operations.

careers.title: Restaurant Manager
careers.learningPath: BS Hotel and Restaurant Management or BS Hospitality Management, then work up from server or kitchen staff to supervisor to manager.
careers.narrative: You keep a restaurant buzzing by managing the kitchen, the floor staff, and the budget all at once. From fast-casual chains in malls to fine dining in BGC, restaurant managers make sure service is fast, food is great, and customers come back. It is a hands-on business role with clear promotion paths.
careers.phSalaryNote: Entry: P22,000–P30,000/month; Experienced: P40,000–P60,000/month; High-end: P80,000–P120,000/month
careers.outlook: Steady demand as food service industry expands in malls, BPO hubs, and tourism areas.
careers.verificationNotes: Distinct from chef (cooking focus) and hotel manager (full property). Focuses on restaurant operations.

careers.title: Flight Attendant
careers.learningPath: Any college degree preferred, plus training from airline academies or cabin crew schools. Height, grooming, and English fluency are key requirements.
careers.narrative: You ensure passengers are safe, comfortable, and welcomed at 35,000 feet. Beyond serving meals, you are trained for medical emergencies and evacuations. Filipino flight attendants are known worldwide for warmth and professionalism, and local airlines are always hiring as travel rebounds.
careers.phSalaryNote: Entry: P25,000–P35,000/month; Experienced: P40,000–P60,000/month; International: P80,000–P150,000/month
careers.outlook: Strong rebound in aviation; Philippine carriers expanding domestic and international routes.
careers.verificationNotes: Distinct from general customer service. Requires specific aviation safety training and certification.

careers.title: Supply Chain Manager
careers.learningPath: BS Industrial Engineering, BS Logistics Management, or BS Business Administration, then experience in procurement or warehouse operations. CPIM or CSCP certifications help.
careers.narrative: You make sure products move from factory to store shelf without delays or waste. In a country of islands, supply chain pros are crucial for keeping groceries, medicine, and electronics available everywhere. E-commerce growth has made this one of the most in-demand business roles.
careers.phSalaryNote: Entry: P25,000–P35,000/month; Mid: P50,000–P80,000/month; Senior: P100,000–P180,000/month
careers.outlook: E-commerce, manufacturing, and retail expansion drive strong demand for supply chain professionals in NCR and CALABARZON.
careers.verificationNotes: Distinct from general business roles. Specific to logistics, procurement, and operations flow.

careers.title: Bookkeeper
careers.learningPath: BS Accountancy, BS Accounting Technology, or TESDA Bookkeeping NC III. Many start as accounting clerks and advance.
careers.narrative: You keep a company's financial records clean, accurate, and up to date so accountants and bosses can make smart decisions. Every small business, school, and nonprofit needs someone who understands debits and credits. It is a steady, detail-oriented job with clear paths to higher accounting roles.
careers.phSalaryNote: Entry: P18,000–P25,000/month; Experienced: P30,000–P45,000/month
careers.outlook: Constant demand in SMEs, accounting firms, and corporate finance departments.
careers.licensureOrCert: TESDA NC / none for degree holders
careers.verificationNotes: Distinct from accountant (existing) which is strategic/analysis and requires CPA. Bookkeeper is transactional recording.

careers.title: Logistics Coordinator
careers.learningPath: BS Logistics Management, BS Industrial Engineering, or BS Business Administration. TESDA warehouse operations courses also help.
careers.narrative: You are the traffic controller of goods, making sure deliveries arrive on time and warehouses do not overflow. From online shopping orders to factory parts, you track shipments and solve delays before they become problems. E-commerce growth means logistics coordinators are needed everywhere.
careers.phSalaryNote: Entry: P20,000–P28,000/month; Experienced: P35,000–P50,000/month
careers.outlook: Booming demand due to e-commerce, delivery apps, and manufacturing supply chains.
careers.verificationNotes: Distinct from supply chain manager (strategic) and warehouse worker (operational). Tactical coordination role.

careers.title: Quality Assurance Analyst
careers.learningPath: BS Information Technology, BS Computer Science, or BS Industrial Engineering, then QA certifications (ISTQB, Six Sigma). Common in IT and manufacturing.
careers.narrative: You check products and software before they reach customers, catching mistakes so brands keep their good reputation. In IT, you test apps for bugs; in factories, you inspect parts for defects. It is a careful, systematic role that fits students who notice details others miss.
careers.phSalaryNote: Entry: P22,000–P30,000/month; Experienced: P40,000–P60,000/month
careers.outlook: Growing in IT-BPM, software development, and manufacturing quality systems.
careers.verificationNotes: Distinct from data analyst (existing) and software engineer. Focuses on testing and quality control.

careers.title: Customs Broker
careers.learningPath: BS Customs Administration or BS International Trade, then PRC licensure exam for Customs Broker.
careers.narrative: You clear imported goods through Philippine ports and airports, making sure paperwork, taxes, and regulations are all correct. Every smartphone, car part, and grocery item that enters the country needs a customs broker. It is a specialized, well-paying role for detail-oriented students.
careers.phSalaryNote: Entry: P25,000–P35,000/month; Experienced: P50,000–P80,000/month; Senior/Own firm: P100,000+/month
careers.outlook: Steady demand due to import-dependent economy and port modernization; licensed brokers are limited in number.
careers.verificationNotes: Distinct from logistics coordinator and supply chain manager. Very specific to customs clearance and import law.

careers.title: Administrative Assistant
careers.learningPath: Any business-related course or TESDA Office Management / Computer Systems Servicing. Many start right after SHS with strong computer and communication skills.
educationPaths: TESDA Computer Systems Servicing NC II
careers.narrative: You are the organizational backbone of every office, keeping schedules straight, files in order, and meetings running smoothly. From government agencies to BPOs to law firms, every workplace needs reliable admin staff. It is a great entry point for students who are organized, friendly, and tech-savvy.
careers.phSalaryNote: Entry: P16,000–P22,000/month; Experienced: P25,000–P40,000/month
careers.outlook: Universal demand across all industries; admin roles are common entry points with clear paths to office management.
careers.verificationNotes: Distinct from HR specialist (existing) which is people-focused. Admin assistant is operations and clerical support.
